analysis.title: Nobody wants to buy (the market is running out of buyers)
key_insights: NDX was rejected at the 200-day moving average. It remains above the latest panic lows, but momentum is weak. The key level is 27k in NDX futures, which was a pivot last autumn and is also where a long-term trendline sits.
Equity vols are spiking again, and the VXN/VIX gap remains wide.
Momentum players are running close to max shorts in NDX (GS data).
CTAs have sold more than $22bn of S&P 500 exposure over the past week (GS).
Deutsche Bank notes a modest rebound in equity positioning, with discretionary investors adding exposure from the bottom of the range. Systematic strategies continued to cut risk.
Elevated realized volatility is forcing systematic funds to cut risk. Vol control and risk parity strategies are estimated to have sold more than $30bn combined over the past week.
Goldman points out that vol control funds could start re-risking in December/January if volatility settles, which could be a meaningful tailwind for equities.
Total net call volume and net bullish options strategies are at their lowest levels in a while (DB).
Call skew stayed flat throughout the latest squeeze, even before the reversal lower. The options market did not buy into the recovery (GS).
risk_factors: Losing 27k in NDX futures could lead to a fast decline.
Elevated realized volatility keeps forcing systematic funds to sell.
Upside options demand is absent, so there is little speculative support for a rebound.
vol_and_positioning: Equity vols are spiking again and the VXN/VIX gap remains stubbornly wide, meaning tech volatility is elevated relative to the broad index.
Momentum players are close to max short in NDX.
CTAs sold more than $22bn of S&P 500 exposure over the past week (GS).
Vol control and risk parity funds are estimated to have sold more than $30bn combined over the past week. Vol control funds could re-risk in December/January if volatility settles (GS).
Discretionary investors added some exposure from the bottom of the range while systematic strategies kept cutting (DB).
Total net call volume and net bullish options strategies are at multi-week lows (DB). Call skew stayed dead through the squeeze and the reversal (GS).
cross_bank_references: Deutsche Bank notes a modest rebound in equity positioning, with discretionary investors adding exposure from the bottom of the range.
As Goldman points out, these funds could start re-risking in December/January if volatility settles down
